sections.html:
Flower Mound owners can accept a cash offer, list on the open market, or sell the house without repairs. Prices here run high: 65.2 percent of homes are valued at $500,000 or more and 31.5 percent between $300,000 and $499,999, so even a modest house is a large transaction.

That is why timing and terms count as much as price. A fast closing can save carrying costs, while a longer listing may bring more money for a well-kept home.

  • Cash sale: quick closing, no repairs, few showings.
  • Agent listing: more buyers, inspection requests, a longer timeline.
  • Sale complicated by an inheritance or a tax problem: fix the title or the tax account first.

The town estimates 81,925 residents in 2025 and projects 110,591 by 2045. Growth was 20.7 percent in the 2010s and slowed to under one percent in 2025. Median household income is $166,219, which tells you buyers here are usually well informed and able to compare.

Lewisville ISD and Argyle ISD serve most of the town. Denton ISD, Grapevine-Colleyville ISD and Northwest ISD cover small areas. Because the line can fall between neighbors, check the district against your exact address before you put it in a listing.

Many buyers are families. Children under 15 are 19.3 percent of residents, while the 55 to 64 group is the biggest age bracket at 15.8 percent. Questions about school lines and roof age tend to come early in a visit.

The town requires short-term rentals to register through a platform run by GovOS and to collect a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax. Registration opened November 20, 2023, and tax collection began December 1, 2023.

Each month's filing is due on the 15th of the following month, including months when no tax came in. Miss the 25th and a 15 percent penalty applies. Interest of 10 percent per year starts accruing 30 days past the due date. A host who pays on time keeps a 1 percent collection fee.

  • Register on the town's GovOS portal.
  • Send questions to the town's short-term rental email address.
  • Keep receipts and exemption records in case of an audit.

For a house that hosted guests, shut down the account and pay the last month's tax before you sell.

sections.h2: Homestead exemptions and the tax cap
sections.html:
Under state rules every school district grants a $140,000 homestead exemption, with an added $60,000 for owners who are seniors or disabled. Other taxing units may adopt an exemption of their own, capped at a fifth of value and no smaller than $5,000. The appraisal district can tell you which ones your units chose.

A separate limit holds the yearly rise in a homestead's appraised value to 10 percent, beginning the year after the exemption is first granted. Seniors and disabled owners also have a school tax ceiling, and part of that benefit can move with them to a replacement homestead in Texas. If you never claimed it, a buyer who closes after January 1 can typically still receive it for the months left in the year.

Before you list, ask the appraisal district what it has on file for the house. A missing exemption may be worth claiming.

Each January 1 a tax lien attaches to the house and stays with it, so delinquent amounts are paid at or before closing. Delay is expensive, since charges grow during the first half of the year. A balance open on February 1 draws 6 percent plus 1 percent interest per month, and the penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1.

A taxing unit's collection lawyer can add up to a fifth of the tax on top. Owners may request a waiver of penalty and interest in writing. In general that means paying within 21 days after learning of the delinquency and applying before the 181st day. Some collectors offer payment plans of up to 36 months for a residence homestead.

Should the house go to a tax sale, redemption rights vary by property type, and homestead land gets a two-year window. Get a payoff figure from the county tax office in writing before you accept an offer, and pass it to the buyer so it is built into the closing.

sections.h2: Why a cash sale can be simpler
sections.html:
When a buyer needs a mortgage, the lender's appraisal, the inspection and the bank's own schedule can each reopen the price. Paying cash takes the bank out of the picture. If your house has deferred repairs, an unclosed rental registration or an open tax balance, that tends to mean fewer surprises between signing and payday.

Certainty costs something, and the price is a lower bid. Request a written net figure from each buyer. Then set it next to what a listing would leave after commission, repairs, and the extra months of mortgage, utilities and tax.

Different buyers ask for different things.

  • Buyers with loans want an appraisal, an inspection and repair credits.
  • Cash buyers ask only for access and a clean title.
  • Any buyer will ask for school boundaries and the age of the roof.

With any offer, go through the settlement statement one line at a time. An amount you cannot place is worth a phone call to the closing office, because mistakes are cheapest to fix before money moves. Request the final figures a day or two early and hold them against the contract. When a buyer wants the appliances, curtains or a backyard shed left behind, put it in writing in the contract itself, and keep a signed copy.

Your closing office can tell you which county clerk handles the parcel. That clerk keeps the liens and releases a title search turns up, and files the new deed once a notary has acknowledged the signature. Fees are set by the clerk, so ask for a quote before closing day.

Before you sign, confirm that the loan payoff, the current year's tax share and any short-term rental tax account are all settled on the closing statement. Keep a copy of every recorded document, and store them with your tax records for future questions from the IRS or a lender.

  1. Order a payoff letter and a tax statement.
  2. Close out any rental registration.
  3. Sign before a notary, with photo identification for every owner on the deed.
  4. Collect your copies after recording.

faqs.q: Is Flower Mound a good place to sell fast?
faqs.a: Buyers tend to be well informed. With a $166,219 median household income and 65.2 percent of homes valued at $500,000 or more, pricing and condition decide how quickly a house sells.

faqs.q: Must an Airbnb-style host register in Flower Mound?
faqs.a: Yes. Short-term rentals register through the town's GovOS portal and remit a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax, with returns due on the 15th of the following month.
Lewisville ISD and Argyle ISD serve most of the town, with Denton, Grapevine-Colleyville and Northwest ISDs covering small areas.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Texas property tax?
faqs.a: Late charges begin on February 1 and step up on July 1. A collection attorney's fee can then be added.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It stays with you only while you live there. A buyer applies for their own after closing and may get it for the rest of that tax year if the prior owner did not receive it.
